title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: Cheon reduction with H-prime semiprime walks, worst-case bound

claims.statement: Setting: BLS12-381 G1, fixed generator P0 of prime order r, d=2^20 (6d divides r-1), input T=A_1=[s]P0 and powers A_i=[s^i]P0 for i<=n with n>=2^20 (only T and A_d are read, so the bound holds for every n>=2^20 including the scoring value n=2^20), s uniform in 1..r-1. Claim: the deterministic classical attack of proof.md recovers s with success probability at least 0.40 over the uniform challenge, using at most 2^116.8665 total target-group-operation equivalents as a maximum over challenges (under H2 and expected O(1)-probe hashing) (one equivalent = one batched incomplete affine G1 addition = 2000 AArch64 instructions, C=2000). The attack is Cheon's reduction to z=s^d in the order-m subgroup H of d-th powers (m=(r-1)/2^20), solved by a baby-step/giant-step whose baby and giant scalars are products a*w of two 'H-primes' (primes q with q^m=1 mod r), every chain advanced by one batched incomplete affine G1 addition per step from a precomputed table, with a 224-bit parity key of the y-coordinate invariant under the six GLV/negation automorphisms, a sharded hash table, and a final d-th root plus mu_d search. N=2^115.6644 elements per side (6N^2/m=0.52). The total includes all preprocessing (H-prime and walk-list searches, tables, chain starts, the challenge-independent baby phase), hash routing, probe/insert, key canonicalisation and walk bookkeeping at an itemised 239 instructions per element (40+30+61+108) charged as 300, false-match processing, verification and output; preprocessing is at most 2^115.87 units and included in the total; peak memory is at most 2^121.4 bytes; there is no nonuniform advice and no quantum step. Disclosed hypotheses: (H1) the 6N^2 ratios x/(u x') are Poisson-like in H, so coverage is 1-exp(-0.52)=0.4055 (0.40 is claimed); (H2) H-primes have density 1/(2^20 ln q) among primes, which affects only preprocessing cost and is charged with a 4x margin; expected O(1)-probe hashing in an idealised sharded cluster whose routing is charged as instructions; the instruction counts are itemised, not measured. The bound is analytic, memory is exponential, toy experiments are evidence only at their stated scale, and this is not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: mode all (the single initial run) executes ledger, coverage and ec with fixed small trial counts. ledger recomputes the production cost ledger and algebraic facts exactly; coverage runs a scalar-level toy of the semiprime baby/giant sets against the Poisson model; ec runs an end-to-end toy on genuine j=0 curves (batched affine walks, parity key, d-th root). Each mode can be rerun separately with more trials. Toy results are evidence at toy scale only, not a production complexity proof.
